content.value_statement: Android teams need consistent Compose patterns for state, navigation, and performance. This skill gives focused guidance for production Jetpack Compose screens and app structure.
actual_capabilities: Lists Compose setup dependencies for a Gradle version catalog.
Explains ViewModel and StateFlow state management patterns.
Shows screen composable structure with stateless content components.
Summarizes performance practices for recomposition and stability.
limitations: Does not inspect or run an Android project by itself.
Uses example versions that may need updates for current Android releases.
Does not replace device testing, profiling, or accessibility review.
Focuses on Compose UI patterns, not full backend or release engineering.

use_cases.title: Start a Compose Screen
use_cases.description: Plan a new Android screen with clear state flow, loading states, and stateless UI components.

use_cases.title: Review State Management
use_cases.description: Check whether ViewModel, StateFlow, events, and side effects are separated cleanly.

use_cases.title: Plan XML Migration
use_cases.description: Map legacy layout behavior into Compose screens, navigation routes, and Material Design 3 components.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Screen Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new Compose feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building an Android screen for [feature]. Suggest the Compose structure, UI state fields, and main events.

prompt_templates.title: Review State Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of ViewModel and UI state design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Compose state management plan for [screen]. Check ViewModel ownership, StateFlow exposure, events, and side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Design Navigation Routes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a multi-screen Compose app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design type-safe Navigation Compose routes for [app flow]. Include destination responsibilities and parameter handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Recomposition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review for a complex UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Compose screen design for recomposition risks. Suggest stability, remember, and derived state improvements.

output_examples.input: Create a profile screen plan with loading, error, and retry behavior.
output: Defines UI state with loading, profile data, and error message fields.
Keeps data loading in the ViewModel and exposes read-only state to the screen.
Passes only state and event callbacks into stateless profile content components.

output_examples.input: Review navigation for home, profile, and settings screens.
output: Uses typed destinations for each route and keeps route arguments explicit.
Places navigation decisions near the app navigation host.
Avoids passing ViewModel instances between child composables.

output_examples.input: Find performance risks in a Compose list screen.
output: Moves repeated expensive calculations out of the composable body.
Uses remembered derived state for values based on stable inputs.
Reviews UI state models for stability annotations and immutable collections.

best_practices: Keep ViewModel state read-only outside the ViewModel.
Pass state and callbacks to child composables instead of passing ViewModel objects.
Use remembered or derived state for expensive values inside composables.
anti_patterns: Do not mutate UI state directly from composable bodies.
Do not perform expensive sorting or filtering on every recomposition.
Do not treat example dependency versions as automatically current.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and review Android Jetpack Compose screens, state management, navigation, and performance practices.

faq.question: Can it migrate XML layouts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide migration planning, but a developer must still implement and test the Compose UI.

faq.question: Does it run Gradle or Android Studio?
faq.answer: No. The skill is instructional and does not run local tools, builds, or emulators.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is the dependency guidance always current?
faq.answer: No. Verify AndroidX and Compose versions against official release notes before implementation.

faq.question: Does it cover backend architecture?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Android UI structure, Compose state, navigation, and related performance guidance.
